purpose: Public-safe, machine-readable source dataset for compiling engineering-practice contracts and per-task applicability profiles.
authority_limit: This registry records original Ranex synthesis and locators. It neither copies the books nor proves that any practice is implemented, effective, applicable to a particular subject, or conformant.

source_families.default_limit: Not a prescriptive lifecycle and not evidence of ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2026 clause conformity.

source_families.title: Code Complete, Second Edition, retained Chapter 5 excerpt
source_families.default_limit: Only the retained excerpt is evidence; absent chapters are out of scope.

source_families.title: Clean Code
source_families.default_limit: Language- and TDD-era heuristics are contextual, and code is not the only Ranex authority.

source_families.title: The Pragmatic Programmer, original first edition
source_families.default_limit: Dated tooling and team advice require current security, provenance, and organizational fit.

source_families.title: System Design Interview, Second Edition
source_families.default_limit: Simplified web-scale examples are prompts, not Ranex topology defaults.

source_families.title: The Clean Coder
source_families.default_limit: Fixed hours, percentages, staffing ratios, and a single development technique are not universal controls.

source_families.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications, Sixth Early Release
source_families.default_limit: The local pre-publication copy is unfinished and excludes security, deployment, operations, ethics, and management; high-consequence claims require final-edition or primary-source confirmation.

source_families.title: Fundamentals of Software Architecture, First Edition
source_families.default_limit: Qualitative ratings and style preferences are contextual and cannot become universal scores.

source_families.title: Clean Architecture, First Edition
source_families.default_limit: Boundary and dependency guidance requires quality-attribute tradeoff analysis; calling a mechanism a detail does not remove its data, security, reliability, or operational constraints.

source_families.title: A Philosophy of Software Design, First Edition v1.01
source_families.default_limit: Experience-based Java/C++ module-design guidance and qualitative depth judgments require subject-specific change, coupling, usability, reliability, security, and performance evidence; they are not a universal scalar design score.

practices.title: Check the whole software-engineering discipline surface
practices.synthesis: Use the knowledge-area map to locate missing requirements, architecture, design, construction, verification, operation, maintenance, configuration, management, process, quality, security, economics, and foundation work.
required_behavior: Record every applicable knowledge area, justified exclusions, owners, and evidence homes.
limitations: Knowledge-area coverage is not lifecycle-process or standards-clause conformity.

practices.title: Trace engineering work through change and quality evidence
practices.synthesis: Treat requirements, design, construction, testing, configuration, maintenance, quality, and management as connected disciplines with explicit trace and change control.
required_behavior: Bind changed requirements to decisions, implementation, tests, release evidence, and maintenance consequences.
limitations: The exact Ranex process and authority model come from accepted lifecycle controls, not this guide alone.

practices.title: Perform explicit, proportionate design during construction
practices.synthesis: Treat construction design as iterative, heuristic, tradeoff-bearing work that may reveal facts requiring controlled design revision.
required_behavior: Record local design alternatives and re-enter material discoveries through normal design/change control.
limitations: Iterative design does not authorize authority, security, persistence, or recovery decisions to emerge accidentally.

practices.title: Separate essential from accidental complexity
practices.synthesis: Make required domain and failure complexity explicit while reducing incidental coupling, duplication, and mechanism leakage.
required_behavior: Name essential complexity and show how the chosen design removes or contains accidental complexity.
limitations: Simplicity cannot omit essential authority, denial, failure, recovery, or lifecycle behavior.

practices.title: Hide volatile decisions behind cohesive interfaces
practices.synthesis: Decompose around owned responsibilities, conceal change-prone mechanisms, and minimize coupling through explicit interfaces and contracts.

locators.section: Chapter 5, information hiding, cohesion, coupling, and interfaces

required_behavior: Assign one owner, expose a narrow contract, and prevent consumers from depending on the hidden mechanism.
limitations: This principle does not prove any particular bounded-context count or directory tree.

practices.title: Wrap volatile and third-party interfaces
practices.synthesis: Keep vendor and external API concepts outside core policy by translating them through owned boundary contracts.
required_behavior: Expose an owned port, translate external types, and test the adapter contract and failure paths.
limitations: A wrapper is not sufficient evidence for security, protocol correctness, or operational recovery.

practices.title: Separate system construction from runtime policy
practices.synthesis: Confine configuration discovery, object assembly, and startup wiring so runtime policy receives validated dependencies instead of discovering global mechanisms.

locators.section: Chapter 11, separating constructing a system from using it

required_behavior: Keep dependency assembly at the composition boundary and reject import-time or environment-presence authority selection.
limitations: Dependency-injection style is a means, not the control objective.

practices.title: Refactor in small verified steps
practices.synthesis: Improve local clarity, cohesion, and duplication only while preserving requirement and regression evidence.
required_behavior: Keep scope bounded and preserve all applicable tests and trace evidence through each refactoring step.
limitations: Local cleanliness cannot compensate for a failed architecture, security, or lifecycle gate.

practices.title: Keep authoritative knowledge in one governed source
practices.synthesis: Eliminate duplicated knowledge by generating or projecting representations from one accepted semantic owner.
required_behavior: Name the semantic owner and generate or validate every duplicate representation against it.
limitations: DRY must not create shared domain ownership, a common database, or a god service.

practices.title: Localize the effect of change
practices.synthesis: Design components so a change in one concern has a small, explicit effect on unrelated concerns.
required_behavior: Declare dependencies and demonstrate that representative changes do not spread through unrelated owners.
limitations: Perfect independence is neither possible nor required; necessary coupling must remain explicit.

practices.title: Preserve viable options and reversal paths
practices.synthesis: Delay avoidable lock-in and design migrations, rollback, and retirement before committing to volatile mechanisms.
required_behavior: Record lock-in, exit conditions, migration path, rollback limits, and retirement consequences.
limitations: Optionality has cost and must be proportionate to a named uncertainty.

practices.title: Use production-shaped tracer routes for learning
practices.synthesis: Build a narrow end-to-end route that exercises real boundaries and yields feedback without treating the route as the complete product.
required_behavior: Route through production-shaped interfaces, capture falsification evidence, and retain the mapped destination and missing coverage explicitly.
limitations: A tracer is not an MVP scope decision, disposable prototype, or permission to leave authority and interfaces undefined.

practices.title: Clarify, decompose, deep-dive, and reconcile
practices.synthesis: Structure architecture work by clarifying scope and quality needs, mapping the whole high-level system, selecting risk-bearing seams for deep analysis, and reconciling tradeoffs and remaining unknowns.

locators.section: A 4-step process for effective system design

required_behavior: Record actors, requirements, scale envelope, complete decomposition, selected deep dives, tradeoffs, and unresolved questions.
limitations: Interview time boxes are not Ranex policy and the method does not prove completeness by itself.

practices.title: Require measured need before adopting scale patterns
practices.synthesis: Use cache, queue, replication, sharding, rate limiting, and multi-region patterns as questions to investigate, not defaults.

locators.section: Scale estimation and high-level design pattern catalogue

required_behavior: Bind a measured load/failure need, consistency model, operating cost, recovery design, and accepted ADR before adoption.
limitations: Simplified interview examples and missing extraction figures are insufficient decision evidence.

practices.title: Co-develop executable acceptance examples
practices.synthesis: Clarify expected behavior with accountable stakeholders using examples that remain traceable to requirements and independent acceptance.
required_behavior: Bind executable examples to owned requirements and preserve independent acceptance authority.
limitations: Examples clarify requirements; they do not replace the requirements, risks, or human decision.

practices.title: Use multiple verification levels selected by risk
practices.synthesis: Combine local, component, integration, system, acceptance, and exploratory evidence according to the subject's failure modes.
required_behavior: Map each material risk to the lowest-cost convincing evidence and retain required integration, security, resilience, and operational proof.
limitations: The book's fixed pyramid percentages and coverage figures are rejected as universal gates.

practices.title: Separate uncertainty estimates from commitments
practices.synthesis: Express forecasts as uncertainty and commit only to controlled actions, named dependencies, and explicit recommitment conditions.
required_behavior: Record forecast range, assumptions, dependencies, capacity authority, risk disclosure, and recommitment triggers.
limitations: Heroic certainty, overtime, and fixed estimation mechanics are not acceptable substitutes for evidence.

practices.title: Define reliability, scalability, and maintainability operationally
practices.synthesis: Translate broad quality labels into fault behavior, quantified load/performance measures, operability, complexity control, and evolvability.

locators.section: Chapter 1, Reliable, Scalable and Maintainable Applications

required_behavior: Define faults, load parameters, performance distributions, operational needs, and evolvability evidence for the exact subject.
limitations: The local copy's Chapter 1 does not supply Ranex security, privacy, release, or management controls.

practices.title: Use monotonic time for elapsed-duration decisions
practices.synthesis: Separate wall-clock timestamps from elapsed-duration measurement and do not compare host-local monotonic values across machines.
required_behavior: Specify the clock source for timestamps, deadlines, elapsed durations, and cross-host comparisons.
limitations: Monotonic clocks do not make lease ownership safe after process pauses.

practices.title: Fence stale workers at every protected resource
practices.synthesis: Issue monotonically increasing epochs and require the state/effect sink itself to reject stale epochs; client-side lease checks are insufficient.

locators.section: Chapter 8, process pauses and fencing tokens

required_behavior: Bind every protected write, tool, budget, mailbox, and external-effect sink to an epoch check enforced beyond the worker.
limitations: The cited model assumes unreliable but honest nodes; authentication, authorization, sandboxing, and hostile-worker controls remain separate.

practices.title: Avoid ungoverned dual writes
practices.synthesis: Commit canonical state and a durable change record atomically where possible, then treat downstream views and consumers as ordered, replayable, lagging derivations.

locators.section: Chapter 11, keeping systems in sync and change data capture

required_behavior: Name the system of record, local atomic boundary, event order, duplicate policy, consumer lag, replay, and reconciliation.
limitations: CDC mechanisms and distributed brokers are examples, not required Ranex technologies.

practices.title: Distinguish proposed commands from accepted immutable events
practices.synthesis: Validate a command before accepting it as a durable event, and make state derivation deterministic with explicit snapshot, replay, retention, and deletion rules.

locators.section: Chapter 11, event sourcing and state derivation

required_behavior: Specify validation, event acceptance, deterministic projection, snapshot authority, replay, consistency, retention, correction, and erasure behavior.
limitations: The source's retain-all-events assumption can conflict with privacy, legal, and bounded-retention obligations.

practices.title: State exact retry and idempotency assumptions
practices.synthesis: Use stable operation identities and atomicity or idempotence to make retries safe, while explicitly reconciling effects that cannot be naturally repeated.
required_behavior: Define operation identity, duplicate detection scope, atomic boundary, retry lifetime, non-idempotent effect handling, and reconciliation owner.
limitations: Do not claim end-to-end exactly-once behavior from a local idempotency mechanism.

practices.title: Define architecture through structure, characteristics, decisions, and principles
practices.synthesis: A topology is incomplete without explicit quality characteristics, decision rationale, and governing design principles.
required_behavior: Bind each material structural choice to named characteristics, decisions, principles, and stakeholder outcomes.
limitations: A named architecture style does not supply the missing characteristics or rationale.

practices.title: Govern characteristics with subject-specific fitness functions
practices.synthesis: Turn important architecture characteristics into observable constraints or tests that detect drift and falsify assumptions.
required_behavior: For each material characteristic, define the metric or invariant, threshold/distribution, subject, cadence, owner, and response to failure.
limitations: A proxy count or one-time document check is not proof of sustained effectiveness.

practices.title: Record the least-worst contextual tradeoff
practices.synthesis: Compare viable alternatives against the exact quality priorities and retain why the selected compromise fits better than the alternatives.

locators.section: Laws of Software Architecture and least-worst architecture

required_behavior: Compare status quo and at least one viable alternative, including benefits, costs, failure modes, reversibility, and falsifiers.
limitations: Generic style ratings do not substitute for Ranex measurements and priorities.

practices.title: Justify component and consistency boundaries
practices.synthesis: Choose component granularity and transactional/communication boundaries from characteristics and coupling, then revisit them as evidence changes.

locators.section: Components, architecture quanta, and boundary tradeoffs

required_behavior: Measure coupling and communication across every proposed boundary and justify its consistency, failure, ownership, and change-locality benefit.
limitations: More components or bounded contexts do not automatically mean better modularity.

practices.title: Keep orchestration from becoming a coupling hub
practices.synthesis: Separate necessary consistency authority from business and technical orchestration responsibilities, and detect excessive central knowledge or communication.
required_behavior: Measure the central component's responsibility set, dependency fan-in/fan-out, change coupling, and cross-boundary communication.
limitations: Central authority can be necessary; the risk is unbounded responsibility and knowledge, not centrality by itself.

practices.title: Select style contextually and record significant decisions
practices.synthesis: Choose topology and interaction style from domain, characteristics, data, organization, and process, then capture context, alternatives, decision, consequences, and compliance evidence.

locators.section: Choosing an architecture style and modular monolith

required_behavior: Use synchronous interaction by default inside the local product unless async has a measured benefit, and record every significant exception with alternatives and fitness evidence.
limitations: The source's qualitative star tables are prompts, not a Ranex scoring model.

practices.title: Make product intent visible in the architecture
practices.synthesis: Organize core policy around owned use cases and domain intent rather than delivery frameworks or technical mechanisms.
required_behavior: Ensure top-level ownership and APIs communicate Ranex capabilities and keep delivery mechanisms outside domain policy.
limitations: Use-case visibility does not prove that one package layout or one object model is universally correct.

practices.title: Draw boundaries to protect policy and preserve options
practices.synthesis: Separate policy from volatile UI, database, framework, and provider choices where the expected change and quality benefit justify the boundary.

locators.section: Chapter 16, Leaving Options Open; Chapter 17, Boundaries and Plugin Architecture

required_behavior: Name the policy protected, volatile decision deferred, boundary cost, allowed dependencies, and change/failure tests.
limitations: A boundary has cost; do not create it solely because the book names a mechanism a detail.

practices.title: Keep mechanism dependencies outside policy
practices.synthesis: Make dependencies point from replaceable delivery and infrastructure mechanisms toward stable application/domain policy through owned abstractions and translated data.
required_behavior: Prevent inner policy from importing outer mechanisms or their generated data formats; translate at the boundary.
limitations: The rule must be reconciled with language, performance, data ownership, and operational constraints rather than applied ceremonially.

practices.title: Do not equate process separation with architecture
practices.synthesis: Judge a service or component boundary by policy separation, dependencies, ownership, change, and failure behavior rather than deployment process count.
required_behavior: Demonstrate policy boundary, independent failure/change benefit, communication semantics, and operating cost before splitting a process.
limitations: Neither a monolith nor a service topology is automatically well-architected.

practices.title: Make boundaries enforceable in code and tests
practices.synthesis: Use language visibility and testing interfaces so declared components actually hide internals and business behavior can be tested without volatile delivery mechanisms.

locators.section: Chapter 34, Package by Component and Organization versus Encapsulation

required_behavior: Restrict internal visibility, expose purpose-specific public and test contracts, and prevent test-only bypass from becoming production authority.
limitations: The source's test API may bypass security for tests; Ranex must isolate that capability so it cannot exist as a production bypass.

practices.title: Detect complexity through its change and comprehension symptoms
practices.synthesis: Treat change amplification, cognitive load, and unknown unknowns as distinct symptoms of dependency and obscurity, then test whether a proposed design contains rather than merely relocates them.
required_behavior: Identify expected change paths, dependencies, facts a maintainer must know, and obscured behavior; require both change-impact evidence and an independent unfamiliar-reader omission challenge.
limitations: The three symptoms are qualitative diagnostic lenses, not an additive or universal architecture score; unfamiliar-reader results depend on subject, task, and reviewer.

practices.title: Prefer modules whose interfaces hide substantial useful complexity
practices.synthesis: Make public interfaces simple, stable, and complete relative to the useful functionality and volatile decisions hidden behind them, while avoiding shallow layer or class proliferation.
required_behavior: Justify each material module, bounded context, and optional layer by the useful complexity it hides and the burden its public interface imposes on consumers; merge or remove shallow indirection without creating unbounded owners.
verification_methods: public API surface and consumer analysis
limitations: Depth is a contextual relationship, not a mandate to maximize module size; god modules, excessive responsibility, authority ambiguity, and hidden failure behavior remain prohibited.

practices.title: Hide each design decision under one semantic owner
practices.synthesis: Localize knowledge of volatile formats, mechanisms, ordering, policy, and failure behavior behind an owned interface, and reject information leakage or temporal decomposition that spreads one decision across modules.
required_behavior: Assign one semantic owner to each material design decision, expose a narrow complete contract, and test that consumers cannot depend on hidden representation, mechanism, ordering, or lifecycle details.
limitations: Information hiding cannot conceal facts required for authority, denial, security, audit, failure, recovery, or operation; those facts need explicit contracts and evidence.

practices.title: Compare multiple designs for significant decisions
practices.synthesis: Before fixing a consequential interface, boundary, or mechanism, sketch more than one viable design and compare interface burden, information hiding, change impact, failure behavior, and quality-attribute consequences.
required_behavior: For each significant architecture decision, compare the status quo and at least two viable shapes, record their costs, failure modes, reversibility, interface burden, and falsifiers, and retain accountable decision authority.
limitations: The effort must be proportionate to decision significance and uncertainty; trivial or readily reversible local choices do not require ceremonial alternatives.
